title: Earthquakes in Pennsylvania
text:
Did you know that the state of Pennsylvania has fault lines that cause earthquakes? Earthquakes happen when large sheets of rock, called tectonic plates, shift underground causing the earth to move and shake. The magnitude of the earthquakes in Pennsylvania is typically very low, so the shaking is rarely ever felt by people.

Seismologists are scientists who study earthquakes. They measure the magnitude of an earthquake using a seismograph. A seismograph measures how strong the movements are in an earthquake. The Richter Scale describes this measurement from 1.0 (very weak and not noticeable) to 10.0 (strongest and most destructive).

title: Alice Fong Yu

A pale yellow sunset means rain is on the way.

An evening rainbow predicts fair weather.

A morning rainbow in the west means rain.

A pre-dawn copper colored sky in the east means rain.

title: Plains
text: Large areas of northern and western Ohio are dominated by plains. The Till Plains encompass most of western Ohio. The Till Plains formed thousands of years ago, when glaciers that once covered Ohio melted. When the glaciers melted, it left behind a rich layer of sediment, or soil-like material deposited by water, wind, or glaciers. This layer of sediment left behind by melting glaciers is called till. The layer of till deposits makes the soil of the Till Plains very good for growing crops. Farmers in this area grow large amounts of corn, grain, and soybeans.

title: Characteristics of South America
text:

title: The Sea
text: The sea was a central component of life in Ancient Greece. The people living both on the peninsula and on the islands used the sea for fishing, transportation, and trade. Because of the many mountains, the people had difficulty traveling on land. They began to spread out among the islands of the sea. There are over 3,000 rocky islands scattered in the Aegean and Ionian Seas. Because of the early troubles with transportation, ancient Greece developed relatively late in history. Other early civilizations in the region, like Egypt and Mesopotamia, had existed for over 1,000 years before the Greek civilization developed.

title: Santiago Sacatapequez, Guatemala
text:
All over the country of Guatemala, people celebrate All Saints' Day by visiting cemeteries and decorating the graves of their loved ones. But in Santiago Sacatepequez, they do something more. The people of this Guatemalan city design and make huge kites, some as large as elephants, and then fly them in the cemeteries of the city.

The people of Santiago Sacatepequez first started flying kites on All Saints' Day many years ago. Some say the reason they first started flying kites was that a magician in their city told them this would scare evil spirits away from the cemetery. title: Blueberry
text:
Blueberries in Maine can be either the highbush or lowbush variety.

The highbush gets to be from 5 to 10 feet tall with leaves that are elliptical, smooth and green. Its blossoms are vase-shaped and vary in color from white to pink. The color of the berries varies from blue to blue-black. It grows best in swamps and moist woodlands

The lowbush gets to be from 3 to 15 inches tall with leaves that are bright green and shiny, and edges that resemble very fine teeth. Its blossoms also vary in color from white to pink. The berries are a blue-black color. It grows well in bogs, tundra and dry sandy flats.

title: The Third Seminole War
text: By the end of the Second Seminole War, about 500 Seminole remained in Florida. They were pushed out of their ancestral homeland and the reservation created in the Treaty of Moultrie Creek and forced to settle in southwest Florida. This area of Florida was very different from the area that the Seminole originally inhabited. This part of Florida is dominated by the Everglades. The Everglades provided protection from invading forces, but it was not an easy place to live. The soil is sandy and very wet, making it difficult to farm. There are also many animal species that are dangerous to humans. Despite these challenges, the Seminole refused to leave Florida.

title: The Ballpoint Pen
text:
When the Pilgrims wrote about their lives in America, they didn't have pens like those that we use today. They used pens made from feathers dipped in ink.

Later, people used fountain pens. These pens were messy and ran out of ink often, and their scratchy points made holes in the paper. Many people tried to make a pen that had its own ink stored inside, but the ink in these pens either clogged or leaked out all over.

In 1938, Ladislo and Georg Biro, two brothers from Hungary, came up with an idea to make the ink in a ballpoint pen flow more smoothly. They created a special rough ball at the end of the pen that worked like a sponge, sucking the ink into the point when someone wrote with it.

title: La tribu Seminola
text:

Los Seminolas acogieron a indígenas americanos de muchas tribus en busca de un nuevo hogar. También acogieron en su tribu a personas que habían escapado de la esclavitud. title: The Fifth Amendment
text:
“... nor shall any person be subject for the same offense to be twice put in jeopardy of life or limb ...”

An individual cannot be tried twice for the same crime. An individual cannot be sentenced (punished) twice for the same crime.

“... nor shall be compelled in any criminal case to be a witness against himself ...” The First Amendment protects the right to speak. The Fifth Amendment protects the right to be silent.

“... nor be deprived of life, liberty, or property, without due process of law …” The government must follow the rules and procedures of the law with no exceptions. Following the legal procedures is called due process.
